question: A 26-year-old woman presents with hair loss. Examination of a single shaft reveals division into two shafts in short segments, with each individually covered with a complete cuticle. What is the most likely diagnosis:
explanation: Pili bifucarti exhibits hair shaft bifurcation into short segments along hair shafts, with each segment covered with it’s own cuticle.

question: This lesion was present at birth. Which opthamologic disease is associated with this disorder?
explanation: Sturge-Weber syndrome is a sporadic disease characterized by a capillary malformation in the trigeminal distribution. Patients may have associated cerebral atrophy, vascular malformations of the leptomeninges, and seizures. All patients with Sturge-Weber should be referred to an ophthamologist for glaucoma screening.

question: A 15-year-old boy presents with keratotic follicular papules involving the bilateral dorsal arms, thighs, and cheeks. Analysis of an unaffected region of skin would likely exhibit which of the following findings:
explanation: Filaggrin mutations are most commonly associated with atopic dermatitis, but have also been implicated in keratosis pilaris as described in this question. Lamellar bodies are diminished in Flegel’s disease and absent in Harlequin icthyosis. Diminished tissue transglutaminase I activity is associated with lamellar icthyosis and non-bullous congenital icthyosiform erythroderma.

question: Compared to children, adults with the condition pictured are more likely to develop which of the following complications?
explanation: Adult patients with Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) are more likely than children to develop persistent renal impairment.

question: A patient presents with thinning of the lateral third of her eyebrows. Which of the following is not associated with this finding?
explanation: The sign of Hertoghe or Queen Anne's sign is a thinning or loss of the outer third of the eyebrows. It is typically seen in HYPOthyroidism not HYPERthyroidism.

question: Increased chylomicrons are a feature of which type of hyperlipoproteinemia?
explanation: Type I (familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency or apoprotein CII deficiency) hyperlipoproteinemia has increased chylomicrons as a feature, and presents with eruptive xanthomas and lipemia retinalis. For the other hyperlipoproteinemias, the associated lipid abnormalities are as follows: Type IIa -- increased LDL; Type IIb -- increased LDL and VLDL; Type III -- increased IDL; Type IV -- increased VLDL. Type V has increased chylomicrons and increased VLDL.

question: The usual culture medium for Mycobacterium leprae is:

choices.B: Agar supplemented with heme and nicotinamide

explanation: M. leprae cannot be grown in media or cell culture. It has been grown in mice footpads and in armadillos. Humans are the only natural host. It is endemic in the tropics and found worldwide.

question: True or relative macroglossia can present in all of the following disorders except:
explanation: Macroglossia is not a feature of Behcet's disease. Behcet's disease presents with oral ulcerations that have recurred at least 3 times in a 12 month period plus 2 of the following: recurrent genital ulceration, eye lesions (posterior uveitis), positive pathergy test, and skin lesions (erythema nodosum, pseudofolliculitis, papulopustular lesions, or acneiform nodules)

question: Chloracne may be secondary to exposure to:
explanation: Chlorinated compounds can cause irritant dermatitis and sometimes chloracne. Chlorinated compounds include chloronaphthalene, chlorodiphenyl, dichlorobenzonitrile, tetrachloroazooxybenzene; dioxin (exposure in the Vietnam war); and cutting oils.

question: A patient presents with a new onset nodule with the following pathology results. They are referred to oncology and started on an FDA approved treatment for this condition. What is the target of this drug?

choices.E: PD-1 receptor on tumor cells ? CTLA-4 receptor on tumor cells ? PD-L1 receptor on tumor cells

correct_text:
PD-1 receptor on tumor cells ? CTLA-4 receptor on tumor cells ? PD-L1
receptor on tumor cells
explanation: This pathology is consistent with a Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC). There are sheets of small round blue cell tumor with high N:C ratio, round / oval nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin (salt and pepper), indistinct nucleoli, and scant cytoplasm. The CD20 stains in a perinuclear dot pattern. Avelumab is a PD-L1 inhibitor, approved for the treatment of MCC. It targets the PD-L1 receptor on tumor cells.

question: A 7-year old girl presents to clinic with onychomadesis afflicting all nails. Her mother reports that she has been healthy other than a self-limited illness two months prior. What is the most likely causative etiology:
explanation: Coxsackievirus, the virus most associated with hand, foot, mouth disease, is a well-known cause of onychomadesis in children.

question: Focal epithelial hyperplasia (Heck’s Disease) is associated with which of the following human papillomavirus types?
explanation: Focal epithelial hyperplasia is caused by HPV-13 and 32.

question: Which type of porphyria disease is most likely to be associated with cholelithiasis?
explanation: Erythropoeitic protoporphyria is caused by a defect in the enzyme ferrrochetalase. Patients present with immediate photosensitivity and subsequently develop waxy scarring on the face, hands and knuckles. In addition to abdominal pain, cholelithiasis and liver disease may also occur.

question: Which PPK is associated with a right-sided cardiomyopathy?
explanation: Naxos is associated with right sided cardiomyopathy. It is an AR, non epidermolytic PPK in which patients have congenital wooly hair and fragile desmosomes. These patients are at risk for heart failure and death.

question: This animal is a nonhuman source of infections for patients for Mycobacterium leprae:
explanation: Leprosy is caused by mycobacterium leprae. Armadillos are a source of nonhuman source for leprosy. They are also transmitted from human to human most likely from respiratory secretions.

question: A 37-year-old woman presents with the fingernail findings pictured. She also has visible deformities of her right elbow that restricts extension. X-rays of the knee and pelvis show absent bilateral patella and the presence of iliac horns; respectively. X-ray of the elbow show bilateral dislocation of the radius. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening test to perform for this patient?
explanation: This patient has nail patella syndrome (NPS), a disorder that presents with the tetrad of fingernail dysplasia, hypoplasia or absence of the patella, presence of iliac horns, and elbow deformities, although ocular, renal, and neurological involvement often exists. Patients are at increased risk of developing kidney disease. There are two patterns of NPS nephropathy, the first is an accelerated age related loss of filtration ability involving the podocytes, the second is the development of nephrotic range proteinuria in childhood or young adulthood that can progress to ESRD. Renal involvement is often diagnosed by the presence of hematuria, proteinuria and microalbuminuria. It can also present with new onset hypertension. Therefore, an annual screening urinalysis should be performed to screen for early indications of kidney involvement.

question: A 52-year-old man presents with pruritic, eczematous plaques and papules with lichenification on his dorsal hands, extensor forearms, V-neck and face that have been persistent for 15 years. There is a sharp cutoff at the line of his shirt. The patient also has a coexisting allergy to daisies. What is the most likely diagnosis of his skin condition?
explanation: 2. Chronic actinic dermatitis is characterized by a chronic eczematous eruption (acute, subacute or chronic lichenified) or pseudolymphomatous lesions in sun-exposed areas. It is most common in men over 50 years of age and commonly affects older men of any race. Positive patch or photopatch tests are common. Coexisting allergic contact sensitivity to plant antigens, fragrances or topical medications is common. The CAD eruption is pruritic, patchy or confluent, and the eczematous lesions can be acute, subacute or chronic in nature; the latter is frequently associated with lichenification. In severely affected individuals, scattered or widespread, erythematous, shiny, infiltrated, pseudolymphomatous papules or plaques may be present in severely affected individuals.

question: Milker’s nodule is caused by infection with which of the following viruses?
explanation: Milker’s nodule is caused by paravaccinia virus, a poxvirus of the genus Parapoxvirus. It is transmitted to humans from infected cows.

question: Fecal isocoproporphyrin is seen in:
explanation: Fecal isocoproporhyrin is characteristic of porphyria cutanea tarda.

question: Which of the following organisms would you expect to recover from a fluorescent tinea capitis?
explanation: M. canis produces a fluorescent ectothrix tinea capitis.

question: An infant presents with poikiloderma on his face, buttocks, arms and legs. He is also noted to have a hypoplastic thumb and no radius. Yearly ophthalmologic examination is indicated because of the infant is at risk for developing:
explanation: The patient described has Rothmund-Thomson syndrome (or poikiloderma congentiale), an autosomal recessive disease localized to chromosome 8 and believed to be due to a DNA helicase mutation (RECQL4). 40-50% of patients will develop juvenile cataracts before puberty. Other clinical features include alopecia, dystrophic nails, short stature, hypogonadism and dental dysplasia.

question: The typical patients with polymorphous light eruption are:

choices.A: Fair-skinned females in their teens and 20's.
choices.B: Type IV-skinned males in their 40's and 50's.
choices.C: Type V-skinned females in their 20's and 30's.

correct_text: Fair-skinned females in their teens and 20's
explanation: PMLE most commonly appears in fair-skinned females during the first three decades of life. It may be related to type IV hypersensitivity.

question: A 37-year-old man presents with a red, tender papule on his lateral right hand that subsequently becomes necrotic with regional lymphadenopathy. An exanthem is also present. Which animal was this individual hunting?
explanation: The presentation described above is that of Tularemia, caused by Francisella tularensis. The most common form of Tularemia is the ulceroglandular form, which is described above. Infected animals, most commonly rabbits, transmit the organism though occasionally tick bites or deer flies may be the vector.

question: Crumpled ears are associated with which disorder?
explanation: Congenital contractural arachnodactyly (also called Beals-Hecht syndrome) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by mutations in fibrillin 2. Affected patients have long limbs, arachnodactyly, scoliosis, and crumpled ears.

question: Sneddon-Wilkinson Disease:

choices.A: Most often occurs in elderly women
choices.C: May occur in association with an IgG monoclonal gammopathy
choices.D: Is usually an acute, self-limited condition
choices.E: Can be treated with narrow band UVB

correct_text: Can be treated with narrow band UVB
explanation: Sneddon-Wilkinson disease, or subcorneal pustular dermatosis, presents with superficial pustules in annular and serpiginous patterns in the axillae, groin, and abdomen. Middle-aged women are most often affected. This condition rarely occurs in association with an IgA monoclonal gammopathy. It is a chronic condition, possibly related to psoriasis, with remissions of variable duration. Treatments including dapsone, acitretin, and narrow band UVB.

question: Which of the following contains significant levels of naturally occurring psoralens?
explanation: Significant quantities of psoralens are present in fruits and vegetables such as limes, lemons, figs, and parsnips. Other furocoumarin (psoralen)- containing plants that can produce phytophotodermatitis are celery, dill, bergamot, parsley, meadow grass, mokihana (lei flowers) berries, mustard, and St. John's wort

question: The most common autoimmune disorder in patients with chronic hepatitis C infection is:
explanation: Autoimmune thrombocytopenia has been reported with hepatitis C infection but not as commonly as autoimmune thyroiditis.

question: How long do hairs stay in telogen before they are released?
explanation: Hairs remain in telogen phase for 3-4 months before they are released.

question: A 74-year-old patient requests the removal of a hyperpigmented plaque with a stuck-on appearance that is rarely bothersome and has been stable for multiple years. Which of the following histopathologic findings are most likely to be discovered after shave removal of the lesion?
explanation: Hallmark histopathologic findings of seborrheic keratoses include acanthosis, papillomatosis, hyperkeratosis, horn cysts, and pseudohorn cysts. In contrast to a common wart, vacuolated keratinocytes are not present in stucco keratoses, a clinicopathologic variant of seborrheic keratoses.

question: A previously healthy 55-year-old patient presents with a four-month history of the pictured indurated papules and plaques. History does not reveal prior skin problems. The lesions started on the cheeks and are now affecting the forehead. The sun seems to exacerbate the condition, causing mild burning and pruritus. Patient complains of cheek swelling that worsens in the morning and improves as the day progresses. Prior treatments included oral doxycycline, sulfur- based face washes, and topical metronidazole, all with minimal improvement. Which of the following medications is most
explanation: The correct answer is isotretinoin. This patient has granulomatous rosacea (GR), a rare subtype of rosacea. Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that affects the central face. UV exposure, spices, stress, exercise, and heat can exacerbate the condition. GR is very challenging to treat, becoming often treatment-resistant to the common topical (metronidazole, azelaic acid) and oral agents (low dose doxycycline at 50 mg/day or less). Since the patient failed to respond adequately to three months of doxycycline, the next best step is the initiation of isotretinoin. The typical isotretinoin dosing for GR is between 0.3-0.5 mg/kg/day. It has been demonstrated that isotretinoin had superior efficacy compared to doxycycline. The mechanism of action of isotretinoin is downregulation of the pro-inflammatory Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) expression on monocytes.

question: A 7 year old boy is seen for "acne". Hypopigmented patches are seen on the trunk and flesh- colored papules are seen around the nails. Biopsy of one of the papules of the face reveals an angiofibroma. A review of his chart reveals that he takes medications for seizures. What is the most common neoplasm associated with the most likely disorder?
explanation: Tuberous sclerosis is an autosomal dominant disorder with seizures, mental retardation, and characteristic skin findings, including hypopigmented macules, facial angiofibromas, periungual fibromas, and collagenomas. The most common associated tumor is renal angiomyolipoma. Rarely, renal cell carcinoma can develop.

question: A 4 year-old boy is diagnosed with Staphylococcal Scalded-Skin Syndrome. Vesiculation in this disease is secondary to exfoliative toxins binding what target protein?
explanation: Staphylococcus Scalded-Skin Syndrome (SSSS) is caused by Staphylococcus exfoliative toxins A and B binding desmoglein 1. This results in the intraepidermal split at the granular layer seen in this illness. Targeting of desmoglein 3 would result in a suprabasilar split. Targeting of plectin, BPAG1, or BPAG2 would result in a subepidermal split. This is not seen in SSSS.

question: Streptobacillus moniliformis is the causative organism of which infectious disease?
explanation: Rat-bite fever (Haverhill fever) is caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis.

question: A patient has multiple erythematous/violaceous psoriasiform dermatitis affecting the ears, nose, hands, and feet and symmetric onychodystrophy. The patient is diagnosed with Bazex syndrome (acrokeratosis paraneoplastica). Which of the following is the best first course of action?

choices.B: Order a TSH and free T4.
choices.C: Obtain a detailed patient history and perform a physical examination.
choices.D: Start topical corticosteroids or topical calcineurin inhibitors.

correct_text: Obtain a detailed patient history and perform a physical examination
explanation: The most important first step is identifying the underlying malignancy. Most often, the skin changes precede cancer symptoms by at least 6 months. The favored therapy to eliminate the described skin lesions is the effective treatment of the underlying tumor. It is the most common treatment modality for this paraneoplastic syndrome and the only clearly beneficial therapy reported so far. Although skin lesions show a fast remission after tumor response, the progress of the malignancy is often associated with relapses of skin manifestations in a short time period. To identify the underlying neoplasm, a detailed patient history and a physical examination are mandatory. Upon suspicion of acrokeratosis paraneoplastica, a diagnostic workup including otolaryngologic examination, chest radiography, a complete blood cell count, an erythrocyte sedimentation rate, a biochemistry profile, tumor markers, and a test for occult blood in stool should be performed. Gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy or radiological workup can follow.

question: Which of the following is true regarding solar urticaria being considered for phototesting?

choices.A: An additional reading at 15 minutes after exposure should be performed
choices.B: Visible light will not evoke the lesions
choices.C: The lower back should not be used for testing
choices.D: An MED (B) and MED (A) should not be performed
choices.E: 7 test squares of increasing UV doses should be exposed

correct_text: An additional reading at 15 minutes after exposure should be performed
explanation: When solar urticaria is a consideration, an additional reading at 15 minutes after exposure is important, as wheals begin within 10-30 minutes after exposure and last for about one hour. The face and hands may not show lesions as they are chronically exposed to sun. Some patients react to either visible light or UVA or UVB. Others react to both UVB and UVA, both UVA and visible light, or all three.

question: A 5-month-old female presents to your clinic with erythematous, hyperkeratotic papules and plaques in baschkoid distribution on the left upper and bilateral lower extremities. Additionally, her mother notes that since birth, the patient has always had an area on the scalp that has been "bald" despite being born with normal hair elsewhere on the scalp. The protein associated with the gene that is mutated in this patient's condition has what function?

choices.B: Facilitates transport of lipid across a membranes

explanation: This patient has incontinentia pigmenti (IP), caused by a mutation in IKBKG, which encodes NF-kB essential modulator (NEMO). NEMO activates NF-kB, a transcription factor that protects cells against apoptotic stimulation by TNF-alpha. The gene is located on the X chromosome; mutation is lethal in XY males and contributes to the Blaschkoid distribution of skin findings due to lyonization. Although inherited in an X-linked dominant fashion, most cases occur due to sporadic mutations. IP typically presents soon after birth with linear, whorled, inflammatory vesiculobullous papules or plaques in Blaschkoid distribution that then, with age, classically progress through verrucous, hyperpigmented and hypopigmented/atrophic stages. Other abnormalities include whorled/linear alopecia of the scalp vertex, nail dystrophy, and dental abnormalities. Patients also have ocular and neurologic involvement.

question: The causative organism for Brucellosis is which of the following:
explanation: Brucella species which cause Brucellosis are gram negative rods. Brucellosis, aka undulant fever, is characterized by an acute febrile illness with headache and joint pain. CNS and cardiac manifestations can also occur. It is acquired by contact with infected animals or contaminated dairy products. Treatment is with doxycycline and rifampin.

question: A 36-year-old woman presents with arthralgias and three fingernails exhibiting adherence of the ventral surface of the distal nail plate to the hyponychium. What is the most likely associated disease:
explanation: The most common cause of ventral pterygium is systemic sclerosis.

question: The major endemic area for Histoplasmosis is?
explanation: The endemic area for Histoplasmosis includes: the Ohio, Mississippi, and Missouri River Valleys, Syracuse NY area, and the Caribbean. This organism prefers soil with a high nitrogen content such as that enriched with bird and bat guano.

question: The patient shown reported significant weakness when standing up or combing her hair over the past several weeks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The answer is dermatomyositis with the heliotrope color and distribution of erythema or violaceous color. The skin over the metacarpal and proximal interphalangeal joints can become inflamed and erythematous forming Gottron papules.

question: Of the following, which one is most characteristic of phototoxicity rather than photoallergy?
explanation: Furocoumarins may cause a phytophotodermatitis that is a phototoxic reaction. Such reactions occur with high frequency in the population, occur within minutes to hours from exposure, and appear like an exaggerated sunburn.

question: A 7-year-old, healthy patient comes to the clinic with the following rash for the last five days. The lesion is slowly expanding. They had recent travel to Minnesota and spent time hiking and camping. Their family does not recall seeing a tick. The patient is otherwise well without systemic symptoms. On examination, there are no other skin lesions

choices.A: Doxycycline 4.4 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily for 10 days
choices.B: Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day orally divided TID for 10 days
choices.C: Doxycycline 4.4 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily for 28 days
choices.D: Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day orally divided thee times daily for 28 days
choices.E: Doxycycline 4.4 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily for 14 to 21 days

correct_text: Doxycycline 4.4 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily for 10 days
explanation: This is erythema migrans, a cutaneous finding of Lyme disease. The patient is uncomplicated without any associated symptoms. Appropriate management for pediatric patients with early, uncomplicated Lyme disease includes the following: - Doxycycline 4.4 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily for 10 days - Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day orally divided three times daily for 14 days - Cefuroxime 30 mg/k/day orally divided three times daily for 14 days Previously, doxycycline was not recommended for pediatric patients under nine due to the risk of discoloration of teeth. However, more recent data support that short courses of doxycycline under 21 days are a safe option.

question: What of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?
explanation: The image displays palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP) which represents chronic sterile pustules over the palms and soles. Many patients who develop PPP have no pre-existing psoriasis. TNF-a inhibitors have been implicated in the development of palmoplantar pustulosis. Acitretin, among other treatments, is a first line option. This image could also represent Generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP), which is a rare and serious skin disorder that presents with flares of widespread sterile pustules on a background of red and tender skin. However, the sole is seen in the photo. Histologically numerous neutrophils are seen in the epidermis. Acitretin is an effective therapy. It may progress to erythroderma and may cause loss of the nails if it progresses to the distal digits. IL-36 inhibitors are a possible advance in the treatment of GPP and PPP.

question: Which autoantibodies are associated with an increased risk of malignancy in dermatomyositis?
explanation: Anti-155/140 has been associated with an increased risk of malignancy in dermatomyositis patients.

question: A 27 year old presents with some mildly itchy spots on his posterior neck. Biopsy reveals elastosis perforans serpiginosa. Other notable exam findings include tall stature, joint laxity, pectus excavatum, and a high-arched palate. Which gene is most likely mutated in this patient?
explanation: Marfan syndrome is a connective tissue disorder that mainly affects the bones and joints (skeletal system), heart and blood vessels (cardiovascular system), and the eyes. Connective tissue is an essential component of the human body as it holds the body together and provides a framework for growth and development. The main characteristic features of the syndrome include: tall and thin stature with long extremities (arms, legs, fingers and toes disproportionately long in relation to rest of the body), eye problems where one or both lenses of the eye may dislocate, heart and blood vessel problems that may result in heart murmurs, irregular heartbeat, or in severe cases aortic aneurysm (potentially fatal heart condition). Other systems that may be affected include the lungs, nervous system and the skin. Marfan syndrome is caused by a defect in the gene on chromosome 15 that determines the structure of fibrillin, a protein that is a major component of elastin-associated microfibrils. These microfibrils are found in most connective tissue but are abundant in large blood vessels and the suspensory ligaments of the lens. Hence the most prominent features of Marfan syndrome are cardiovascular (heart) and ocular (eye) abnormalities.

question: A 40 year-old man presents with a slow-growing, large, firm, nodular tumor on the back. Immunohistochemical staining of the biopsy specimen from this tumor is positive for CD34 and negative for Factor XIIIa. The patient subsequently undergoes wide excision with adjuvant chemotherapy. Which of the following chemotherapeutic agents was most likely used?
explanation: Imatinib has been used in the treatment of primary or locally recurrent dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. Even with wide excision, the 5 year recurrence rate for this tumor can be 20-25%. This neoplasm commonly possesses a reciprocal translocation t(17;22) resulting in fusion of collagen 1alpha1 and platelet derived growth factor B (a fusion oncogene). Activation of the platelet derived growth factor receptor associated with overexpression of platelet derived growth factor is central to the development of DFSP. Imatinib is a protein tyrosine kinase inhibitor used primarily to treat chronic myelogenous leukemia with the Philadelphia chromosome defect. Imatinib also inhibits the tyrosine kinases associated with platelet derived growth factor and stem cell factor. Therefore, it directly inhibits the platelet derived growth factor receptor signaling cascade, which plays a critical role in the pathogenesis and growth of DFSPs. While Imatinib has been successful in clinical trials, it is not yet FDA-approved for the treatment of DFSP. DFSP stains positive for CD34 and negative for Factor XIIIa, which differentiates it from a dermatofibroma (stains positive for Factor XIIIa and negative for CD34).

question: A 48-year-old Latin American female with a diagnosis of leprosy develops vasculitic lesions that appear rapidly and ulcerate, especially below the knee. This most likely represents:
explanation: This patient has a type III reactional state to leprosy called Lucio's phenomenon. It mostly occurs in people of Latin American descent and is characterized by rapidly ulcerating vasculitic lesions usually on the legs. It has a high mortality rate.

question: A 32 year old male patient presents with the sudden eruption of multiple itchy bumps on his feet after playing with his children in the grass. Hydrocortisone is improving the itchiness somewhat. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The patient has encountered chiggers, mite larvae who feed on human keratinocytes. Their feeding process induces the development of the characteristic chigger bite, which is very pruritic. Topical steroids can reduce the itch sensation.

question: Adenosine deaminase deficiency is seen in which immunodeficient disease?
explanation: Severe combined immunodeficiency is a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by decreased humoral and cell mediated immunity. Patients may have recurrent infections including cutaneous ones, GVHD (due to in utero cmaternal lymphocytes), sepsis, oral candidiasis, and diarrhea. Implicated genes include the IL-2 receptor (x-linked recessive form) and adenosine deaminase deficiency (autosomal recessive form).

question: Which of the following plant families commonly causes phytophotodermatitis?
explanation: The Apiaceae family (formerly Umbelliferae) includes parsley, celery, parsnip, hogweed, and fennel, all potential causes of phytophotodermatitis.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding ultraviolet carcinogenesis?

choices.A: UVA, when added to UVB, may accelerate carcinogenesis
choices.B: Suppressor T-cells arise in UV-irradiated hosts only after tumors have developed
choices.C: Cells from patients with actinic keratoses have normal DNA repair capacity
choices.D: UVA is most effective in producing pyrimidine dimers, which may activate oncogenes
choices.E: Mid-range ultraviolet radiation is less efficient in inducing neoplasia in mice that is long wave UVR

correct_text: UVA, when added to UVB, may accelerate carcinogenesis
explanation: Mid-range UVR (280-320 nm) is more efficient in inducing neoplasia in mice, but long wave UVA, when added to UVB, may accelerate carcinogenesis.

question: Which of the following is a clinical manifestation of neonatal lupus erythematosus:
explanation: Neonatal lupus involves annular scaling macules and plaques appearing within the first few months of life in babies born to mothers with LE or other autoimmune connective tissue diseases. In addition to the rash, babies display congenital heart block, hepatic disease, and thrombocytopenia.

question: Which of the following is the most likely cause of the shown finding in a 36-year-old woman?
explanation: Appreciate the trichoscopic findings of trichorrhexis nodosa, which shows nodular thickenings of the hair with splayed ends into multiple small fibers, as circled. There are myriad causes of this condition, but in a 36-year-old woman, acquired trichorrhexis nodosa from hair damage (eg, heat styling) should be high on the differential. Counseling to avoid these practices is essential.

question: Which of the following cytokines is most characteristic of atopic dermatitis in its chronic phase?
explanation: While acute atopic dermatitis is a TH2 state, chronic eczematous AD is most often a TH1 cytokine environment with interferon-gamma being the best choice.

question: A patient develops full-thickness acantholytic lesions in intertriginous areas with negative immunofluorescence studies. Alterations in ion transport involving which of the following intracellular organelles is most likely?
explanation: Full-thickness acantholysis in the axilla is consistent with the presentation of Hailey-Hailey disease (benign familial pemphigus). The mutation in this disease (ATP2C1) encodes a calcium-manganese transporter of the Golgi apparatus, which is believed to be the underlying cause of acantholysis.

question: A 43 year-old man presents with suppurative nodules and sinus tracts over the mandible. He also is noted to have poor oral hygiene. What is the most likely causative organism?
explanation: Actinomyces israelii is an anaerobic gram-positive rod which causes chronic suppurative nodules and sinus tracts with an exudate containing sulfur granules. It most commonly effects the cervicofacial area, especially near the mandible. The abdomen and thoracic areas can also be affected. The source of infection is endogenous and patients with poor oral hygiene, penetrating foreign bodies, and recent dental procedures are at increased risk. Treatment of choice is penicillin.

question: What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient with a monoclonal gammopathy?
explanation: The patient has necrobiotic xanthogranuloma (NXG) associated with a monoclonal gammopathy, which is most often an IgG kappa or lambda monoclonal gammopathy. NXG is a rare, chronic, progressive granulomatous disorder. It manifests as yellowish plaques and nodules most commonly in the mid face to periocular region.

question: Which of the following is the main irritant found in garlic?
explanation: Thiocyanates are the main irritant found in garlic, black mustard, and radish.

question: Mutations in hair keratins hHB6 and hHB1 cause this characteristic finding pictured below – name the condition:
explanation: Mutations in the hair keratins, hHB6 and hHB 1 cause monilethrix.

question: A 52-year old male develops a brownish-red plaque on his forehead. The lesion has an "apple jelly" color on diascopy, and the patient has a positive PPD skin test. What is the most likely mechanism of disease in this patient?
explanation: This patient has lupus vulgaris, a pauci-bacillary manifestation of tuberculosis infection. Lesions occur in sensitized patients with a moderate to high immune response and are due to hematogenous, lymphatic, or contiguous spread from a distant site of infection. Lesions typically occur on the head and neck. "Apple jelly" color on diascopy is described in lupus vulgaris, but can also be seen in cutaneous lesions of sarcoidosis.

question: Which anticonvulsant and which HLA type would you screen for in Asian patients for high risk of this potential complication?
explanation: The correct answer is A. Han Chinese, Malaysian, and Thai populations are at a significantly higher risk of carrying the HLA-B1502 allele and developing SJS/TEN from carbamazepine (but not Japanese or Caucasians).

question: A 6-year old girl with atopic dermatitis presents with patchy non-scarring alopecia and nail pitting. You make the diagnosis of alopecia areata. What portion of the nail unit is responsible for her nail plate pitting:
explanation: The proximal nail matrix produces the dorsal nail plate. Defective keratinization in this region is therefore responsible for the pitting seen in alopecia areata, psoriasis, eczema, and other cutaneous diseases.

question: A child presents with fever, cutaneous tenderness, and erythema of flexural and periorificial areas. Within 24 hours the erythema progresses to flaccid blisters and erosions. No organisms are cultured and Nikolsky's sign is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Staph scaled skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B (ET-A and ET-B) produced by S. aureus (phage group II, types 71 and 55 most common). Toxins disseminate via blood stream leading widespread cleavage of desmoglein 1. Desmoglein 1 is the specific receptor for exfoliative toxin A cleavage. SSSS is more common in neonates and children as they have an undevelooped immune system to prodcue antibodies against ETs and inadequated renal capacity to excrete the pathogenic toxins. Histopathology of the skin shows superficial intraepidermal splitting without epidermal necrosis with very few inflammatory cells.

question: This condition has which type of inheritance pattern?
explanation: This patient has neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), which has an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern.

question: Phytophotodermatitis due to skin exposure to limes is caused by:
explanation: Phytophotodermatatitis (phototoxic eruptions from plants) are relatively commonly seen in florists, nursery personnel, gardeners, and farm workers. Plants that cause this eruption produce photoxins known as furocoumarins. Fig, fennel, lime, lemon, parsley, celery, dill, and hogweed are all causes of phytophotodermatitis.

question: What condition most likely describes a hair defect with ruffled cuticle in 4-year old female with blonde hair?
explanation: Loose anagen hair syndrom occurs primarily in young, females with blond hair. The defect results in early keratinization of the inner root sheath which leads to poor anchoring. Examination of hair shaft reveals ruffled proximal cuticle.

question: The most common ocular association with cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenital is:
explanation: Glaucoma is the most common associated eye finding in CMTC patients. Glaucoma is also seen in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 and Sturge Weber patients.

question: Regarding the UVR effects on contact dermatitis and delayed-type hypersensitivity, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: There are diminished contact hypersensitivity responses
choices.B: There are increases in production of Th2 type cytokines
choices.D: There are increased delayed-type hypersensitivity responses
choices.E: Mice exposed to long-term, high-dose UVR demonstrate increased splenic APC function

correct_text: There are diminished contact hypersensitivity responses
explanation: Mice exposed to short-term, high-dose UVR demonstrate diminished delayed-type hypersensitivity and contact hypersensitivity responses.

question: This condition is transmitted by what vector?
explanation: This photo depicts Leishmaniasis and is transmitted by the sandfly. These are obligate intracellular parasites that are more commonly found in the Middle East and South America. South-central Texas is the only endemic area in the USA. Varying forms of Leishmaniasis can be caused by Leishmania major, L. tropica, L. infantum, L aethiopica, L. mexicana, and L. braziliensis. The sandfly is also the vector for Oroya fever/Carrion's disease.

question: Retention of primary teeth is a prominent dental finding of which of the following conditions?
explanation: Hyper-Immunoglobulin E syndrome is an autosomal dominant condition with impaired regulation of IgE function and deficient neutrophil chemotaxis. There is increased susceptibilty to infections and increased IgE serum levels. Retained primary teeth and lack of development of secondary teeth are characteristic findings.

question: The diagnostic test for chronic granulomatous disease is:
explanation: Chronic granulomatous disease is characterized by a defect in the ability to kill catalase positive organisms within phagocytic leukocytes. This results from a neutrophilic defect in the cytochrome found in the NADPH oxidative pathway responsible for a respiratory burst. The nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) reduction assay demonstrates the leukocyes ability to reduce the dye and produce a blue color change. Patients with chronic granulomatous disease are unable to reduce the dye.

question: Which of the following statements regarding phototesting is correct?

choices.A: The UVA MED is performed using a narrowband UVA source
choices.B: Repeated MEDs to UVB or UVA, given to different test sites over several days can be used to reproduce lesions of polymorphous light eruption
choices.C: A single large dose of visible light is the best way to reproduce lesions of polymorphous light eruption
choices.D: To test for a visible light reaction, a slide projector is used as a light source
choices.E: The UVB MED is performed using narrowband UVB light sources

correct_text: To test for a visible light reaction, a slide projector is used as a light source
explanation: Phototesting is done prior to initiating phototherapy or during provocative induction. To test for a visible light reaction, a slide projector is used as a light

question: The best substrate for indirect immunofluorescent for pemphigus foliaceous is:
explanation: The best indirect immunofluorescent substrate for pemphigus foliaceous is guinea pig esophagus. Pemphigus foliaceous has antigens against desmoglein 1 and typically presents as erosions on the chest.

question: Which of the following may produce red lunulae?
explanation: Red lunulae may be associated with the following: alopecia areata, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus erythematosus (both systemic and cutaneous), congestive heart failure, and carbon monoxide poisoning.

question: A 59 year old African American woman presents with the following lesion. She states she is currently applying topical clobetasol and takes oral hydroxychloroquine, prednisone, and mycophenolate daily. She is interested in discussing ways to improve the appearance of this lesion. Which of the following is NOT true?

choices.A: Disease reactivation after reconstructive filler injection is high.
choices.B: Patient can undergo treatment with pulsed dye laser and Q-switched neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet or for lesions that remain active
choices.D: Fat transfer for atrophic lesions can be performed when disease is inactive and patient is off immunosuppressive medications.
choices.E: Systemic prednisone is associated with poorer outcomes after fat transfer . ? Patient should contine with strict photoprotection given the photosensitive nature of her disease.

correct_text: Disease reactivation after reconstructive filler injection is high
explanation: There are no reports in the literature of lupus reactivation after reconstructive injectable treatment.

question: Electron microscopic examination of a hair shaft reveals a canal-like groove along the shaft of a triangular-shaped hair. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Pili trianguli et canaliculi is also known as spun-glass hair and is associated with uncombable hair syndrome.

question: Which syndrome is characterized by multiple keratoacanthomas beginning in childhood?
explanation: Ferguson Smith is familial (AD), and is characterized by regressing keratoacanthomas beginning in childhood. Grybowski is a non-familial disorder in which patients develop generalized eruptive keratoacanthomas beginning between age 40 to 60. Keratoacanthoma centrifugum marginatum is most commonly a solitary lesion occurring later in life. Muir Torre is a syndrome characterized by gastrointestinal or genitourinary neoplasms which precede development of sebaceous neoplasms and keratoacanthomas by one to two decades. Rombo is not associated with keratoacanthomas, but is associated with multiple basal cell carcinomas, atrophoderma vermiculatum, hypotrichosis, and milia.

question: You are consulted on a patient with possible Nethertons Syndrome. Which location of the body would most likely have hairs demonstrating trichorrhexis invaginata?
explanation: Eyebrow hair is a high yeild site with hairs demonstrating trichorrhexis invaginata.

question: Which of the following is the most likely cause of photosensitivity?
explanation: Doxycycline is the tetracycline derivative most likely to cause photosensitivity.

question: The best first line treatment for dermatitis herpetiformis is:
explanation: The most effective drug for dermatitis herpetiformis is dapsone. The dose varies between 50 and 300 mg daily. Side effects include hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, methemoglobinemia, and rarely agranulocytosis or peripheral neuropathy. Sulfapyridine is also a very effective treatment for dermatitis herpetiformis.

question: This woman is being treated for corticosteroid-induced rosacea with topical metronidazole and an oral tetracycline. She is very concerned about the redness of her face. Judicious use of what color concealer can reduce the appearance of redness on the skin?
explanation: This slide shows a woman with rosacea. Green and red are on opposite sides of the color wheel and thus can “cancel” each other out. Green concealer can neutralize redness on the skin.

question: A 15-year-old boy with type I diabetes presents with erythema, pruritus, and blistering where he normally wears his continuous glucose monitor. What is the most likely contact allergen implicated?
explanation: Should be classified under "Eczematous Disorders" category; however this radio button is missing above. Diabetic devices including glucose monitoring systems and insulin pumps are increasingly recognized as a source of irritant contact dermatitis (ICD) and allergic contact dermatitis (ACD). Isobornyl acrylate is a chemical used in the glue of some of these devices and has been implicated as a frequent culprit allergen in patients who become sensitized to their device.

question: A 39 year old female has noticed a darkening area on both of her ears over the course of several decades. She denies supplement or medication intake and she does not use any topical products; otherwise she endorses a history of joint pains and stiffness. On physical exam, she has darkening of the anti-helix of both ears. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The patient has alkaptonuria. The ears are a common site of involvement and show visible darkening over time. The musculoskeletal system can be involved as well.

question: Scalp biopsy of which of the following types of hair loss will reveal increased telogen hairs?
explanation: Androgenetic alopecia, telogen effluvium, and alopecia areata all have an increased fraction of telogen hairs.

question: The constellation of erythema nodosum, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, uveitis, fever, and arthritis in patients with sarcoidosis is known as:
explanation: The presence of EN, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, uveitis, fever, and arthritis in patients with sarcoidosis is known as Lofgren's syndrome.

question: A sporadic mutation affecting transcriptional coactivator cAMP response element-binding protein produces which syndrome?
explanation: Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome is caused by a sporadically transmitted defect in transcriptional coactivator cAMP response element-binding (CREB) protein. This gene is responsible for encoding a nuclear protein, which acts as a coactivator of cAMP-regulated gene expression. Findings of this syndrome include capillary malformation, short stature, broad thumbs, craniofacial abnormalities including a beaked nose, mental retardation, strabismus, congenital heart defects, and cryptorchidism.

question: An elderly gentleman with a history of hypertension and a thymoma, presents to the Emergency Room with oral and conjunctival erosions and hemorrhagic bullae on his hands and feet. These finds are seen in:
explanation: Paraneoplastic pemphigus is usually associated with cancers of lymphoid origin, including lymphoma, leukemia, thymomas, Castleman's tumor. Clinically, this condition may present with intractable staomatitis, severe painful oral and conjunctival erosions.

question: A child presenting with the scalp findings shown and right arm hypoplasia would be diagnosed with which of the following syndromes?
explanation: Adams-Oliver syndrome is defined by aplasia cutis congenita (ACC) (shown in the image), usually of the midline scalp with limb hypoplasia.

question: Industrial acne can be caused by insoluble oils seen on the scalp, malar cheeks and scrotum. All of the following have been known to cause acneiform eruptions except:
explanation: Tazarotene is a topical retinoid used to treat acne.

question: A 4-year-old boy presents with generalized white scale. The mother reports that her son was born with a tight membrane enveloping his body. Peripheral blood smear is within normal limits. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The most likely diagnosis given the colloidon baby phenotype and subsequent generalized white scale is congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.

question: The best diagnostic test for Cushing syndrome is:
explanation: The overnight dexamethasone suppression test is the test of choice for diagnosis of Cushing syndrome. In this test, a dose of dexamethasone is given at 11pm and the plasma cortisol level is drawn the following morning. If the Cushing syndrome is from an adrenal tumor or an ectopic ACTH producing tumor, there is no change in cortisol secretion. A normal response is suppression of the cortisol level by the extra dexamethasone. If the Cushing syndrome is from a pituitary tumor, at low doses of dexamethasone there are no changes in cortisol levels while at high doses of dexamethasone there will be a normal suppression. The other listed items are not used for diagnosis of Cushing syndrome.

question: All of the following cytokines have demonstrated therapeutic benefit in the treatment of melanoma EXCEPT:
explanation: IL-10 has been used to treat inflammatory disorders such as atopic dermatitis and psoriasis.

question: The Jarisch-Herxeimer reaction is most closely associated with the release of which of the following cytokines?
explanation: TNF-alpha. The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is associated with increased plasma concentrations of TNF-alpha after antibiotic treatment of syphilis. The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction has also been described following treatment of louse-borne relapsing fever, lyme disease and leptospirosis.

question: A 23-year-old man presents for evaluation of an ulcerated plaque on his left eyelid, as shown. He recently arrived with his family from Mexico. A biopsy of the lesion is performed, which is also shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The presence of an ulcerated plaque and the pathology shown given the patient’s recent travel is suspicious for leishmaniasis. Note the pathology findings of the classic "marquee" sign, where the tiny organisms line up in the periphery of histiocytes.

incorrect_rationales.D:
Sarcoidosis

?. Pyoderma gangrenosum

?. Chagas disease

question: Patients with neurofibromatosis type I who also have juvenile xanthogranulomas are at increased risk for developing which of the following?

choices.E: Medullary carcinoma of the thyroid gland

explanation: Patient with NF 1 who have multiple juvenile xanthogranulomas are at 20 times greater risk for developing juvenile chronic myelogenous leukemia.

question: A 31-year-old man with a history of inflammatory bowel disease managed with diet presents with a new ulcerated plaque on his abdomen. A biopsy of the lesion is performed, which is shown. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment for the patient’s skin lesion?
explanation: The treatment of cutaneous lesions of Crohn's disease can be managed first with topical corticosteroids.

question: A 7-year-old female presents with non-painful thickened “rock-hard” skin which started on the left thigh but has since began involving the left buttock. Thickened skin was noticed during infancy but has progressively worsened. Skin overlying the thickened area appears normal. Histology reveals normal epidermis but mild dermal thickening, no inflammation, swollen bundles of collagen oriented horizontally, increased fibroblasts, and adipocyte entrapment. Her mother and maternal grandfather also have the same diagnosis. The pathogenesis of this skin condition involves increased signalling of which of the following?
explanation: This patient has Stiff Skin syndrome (SSS) characterized by the bilateral, thick, hard, and progressive skin induration. Adipocyte entrapment and thick collagen bundles on biopsy confirm this. Various locations may be affected including buttocks, thighs, shoulder girdle, and legs, with involvement spreading to multiple locations with age. The family history suggests an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance; the FBN1 gene leads to fibrillin 1 defect and subsequently increased signalling of TGF-β, leading to a scleroderma-like presentation with excess microfibrillar deposition and defective elastogenesis. Complications of this sclerosis include impaired mobility, restrictive lung disease, and joint contractures.

question: A 14-year-old female presents with the sudden onset of the skin findings pictured diffusely covering greater than 90% of her skin surface. The rash is accompanied by a high fever (40C) and elevated white blood cell count. What is the most likely cause of her condition?

choices.C: Deficiency of the IL-36 receptor antagonist

correct_text: Deficiency of the IL-36 receptor antagonist
explanation: The patient presents with generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP) secondary to deficiency of the IL-36 receptor antagonist (DITRA). IL-36R antagonist is in the IL-1 family and antagonizes proinflammatory IL-36. DITRA has been shown to cause familial and sporadic GPP as well as localized acrodermatitis continua of Hallopeau. It is inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. It accounts for 21-82% of cases of GPP. DITRA has a younger age of onset and higher risk of systemic inflammation compared to non-DITRA GPP.

question: The most common location for primary mucinous carcinoma is:
explanation: Mucinous carcinoma presents as a slowly growing, asymptomatic, round, erythematous nodule on the head and neck. Forty percent of cases occur on the eyelid. Histologically it is characterized by the presence of large areas of mucin ('sea of mucous') with small islands of basophilic epithelial cells. Primary mucinous carcinoma of the skin has an indolent course. Local recurrence occurs in 1/3 of patients following excision. The rate of metastasis is low (9.6%).

question: A patient with HIV/AIDS presents complaining of an asymptomatic patch on the tongue. Examination reveals a white patch with a corrugated surface on the lateral tongue. What percentage of HIV patients will have this finding?
explanation: Oral hairy leukoplakia is characterized by a white patch with a corrugated surface on the side of the tongue. It is generally asymptomatic. Oral hairy leukoplakia is seen most commonly in patients with defective cell-mediated immunity, in particular HIV infection. Oral hairy leukoplakia is associated with EBV opportunisitc infection, among other viruses. 33% of patients with HIV will have oral hairy leukoplakia.

question: Numerous umbilicated nodules resembling molluscum contagiosum developed in a patient with recently diagnosed HIV infection. Which of the following fungi might be the causative agent(s)? 1. Candida tropicalis 2. Cryptococcus neoformans 3. Aspergillus fumigatus 4. Histoplasma capsulatum 5. Penicillium marneffei
explanation: These three organisms can produce molluscum-like lesions in AIDS patients.

question: A 27-year-old Chinese male presents to the emergency department with diffuse, painful sloughing erosions and ulcers involving the mucosa, conjunctiva, and 5% of the body surface area. He admits starting a new medication, Carbemazepine, 2 weeks ago for a seizure disorder. Which of the following HLA types may be associated in this case?
explanation: The condition described in this vignette is Steven-Johnson Syndrome (SJS). HLA-B*1502 has been linked with SJS due to carbamazepine in Han Chinese. In addition, HLA-B*5801 and HLA- A*0206 are associated with SJS/TEN secondary to allopurinol use in Hans Chinese and NSAID use in Japanese/Korean population, respectively. Ueta M. Cold medicine-related Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis with severe ocular complications-phenotypes and genetic predispositions.

question: Ophthalmia nodosa may result following injury by which of the following creatures?
explanation: Tarantulas are relatively large, hair spiders belonging to the Theraphosidae family. Many are kept as household pets given their longevity (they may live to 20 years or more) and slow-moving, relatively sedentary lifestyle. However, when agitated, tarantulas may engage in rubbing their hind legs against their abdomen, resulting in release of numerous urticating, barbed hairs. These projectile hairs may then lodge in the conjunctiva, cornea, iris, or even retina, resulting in multifocal and chronic granulomatous inflammation known as ophthalmia nodosa. Similar reactions may be seen secondary to ocular penetration of the sensory setae of caterpillars.

question: 40-year-old patient referred to dermatology for a rash. The patient is undergoing evaluation for interstitial lung disease (ILD) with worsening shortness of breath (SOB). Review of system is positive for SOB, skin tightness, cold sensitivity, and initially swollen fingers. Based on the clinical images, which autoantibodies is associated with the worst overall prognosis?

choices.E: Anti-U3 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U3-RNP) ? Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)

explanation: The correct answer is Scl-70. The patient has diffuse cutaneous scleroderma/systemic sclerosis (dcSSc). Scleroderma (SSc) is classified as either limited (lcSSc) or dcSSc. This is a case of dcSSc because of the following features: skin thickening affecting the proximal and distal extremities, salt and pepper leukoderma, joint contractures, sclerodactyly, digital tip ulcers and pitting scars. Generally, dcSSc with Scl-70 has the worst prognosis, with 46.5% survival at 20 years; Scl-70 is associated with high risk of early ILD, scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) and cardiac involvement.

question: This insect transmits which of the following diseases?
explanation: Malaria, the most common parasitic disease in the world, is transmitted to the human host by mosquitoes of the genus Anopheles.

question: This autosomal dominant condition is characterized by trichodiscomas, fibroepithelial polyps, and fibrofolliculomas:
explanation: Birt-Hogg-Dube is an autosomal dominant condition characterized by trichodiscomas, fibroepilethial polyps and fibrofolliculomas.

question: A 24-year-old man with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is most likely to present with what nail disorder:
explanation: Oncyhophagia refers to nail biting. Patient’s with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, caused by defective HGPRT enzyme, are prone to self-mutilating behaviors, including onychophagia.

question: A 6-year-old boy presents with brachyonychia and three firm subcutaneous nodules with a bluish hue on the trunk. Biopsy of a representative lesion is consistent with a pilomatricoma. What is the most likely associated syndrome?
explanation: Rubenstein-Taybe syndrome is caused by a amutation in CREB-binding protein and presents with brachyonychia, eruptive keloids, and multiple pilomatricomas.

question: Exanthem subitum (ie, roseola infantum) is caused by which of the following?
explanation: Exanthem subitum (roseola infantum, sixth disease) is caused by human herpesvirus 6 and 7 (HHV-6 and HHV-7).

question: A patient is diagnosed with a unilateral enlargement of the medial clavicle after being diagnosed with congenital late syphilis. This is called the:
explanation: This patient has congenital late syphilis, seen in children over two years of age. The unilateral enlargement of the medial clavicle is called the Higoumenaki's sign. These patients also can have Hutchinson's teeth or widely-spaced, peg-shaped teeth in the upper incisors. They can also have a saddle nose and saber shins.

question: Which HPV serotype has been associated with periungual SCC?

choices.B: HPV is not associated with SCC

explanation: HPV infection has been associated with the development of cutaneous SCC. HPV 16 has been found in periungual SCC.

question: Which of the following is TRUE regarding this lesion?

choices.A: Female gender is a poor prognostic factor
choices.B: It is the most common type seen in darker-skinned patients
choices.C: Ulceration is the most important prognostic factor
choices.D: Immunosuppression is not a risk factor
choices.E: Anti-PD-1 antibodies are not helpful in treatment

correct_text: It is the most common type seen in darker-skinned patients
explanation: The associated image depicts an acral lentiginous melanoma (ALM), which is the most common type of melanoma in darker-skinned individuals. Notably, and very sadly, the famous musician Bob Marley was diagnosed with ALM in 1977 and succumbed to this malignancy in 1981 as it had metastasized to his lungs and brain.

question: In chronic granulomatous disease, the diagnosis is made by which of the following tests?
explanation: Chronic granulomatous disease (CGD) is diagnosed by the nitroblue tetrazolium reduction assay. The abnormal white blood cells cannot reduce dye due to the inability to produce the respiratory burst. This is needed to kill catalase positive organisms after phagocytosis.

question: A 16 year old female presents with a sore throat, painful cervical lymphadenopathy, and an enlarged spleen. An empiric trial of amoxicillin leads to the development of a diffuse morbilliform rash. What is the incubation period of the most likely viral cause of this patient's symptoms?
explanation: Infectious mononucleosis is characterized by a sore throat, painful lymphadenopathy, fatigue, and splenomegaly. The formation of a morbilliform rash upon challenge with ampicillin or related antibiotics is a classic finding. The most common virus associated with infectious mononucleosis is Epstein-Barr virus. The incubation period is relatively long, 3-7 weeks.

question: A 64-year-old female patient presents with an intensely itchy rash on the shins, thighs, feet, and forearms. The lesions consist of multiple raised papules that are scaly and reddish-brown. The papules may coalesce into thickened plaques. What is the most likely diagnosis for this condition?
explanation: The clinical scenario describes lichen amyloidosis. Lichen amyloidosis is derived from keratin and is the most common form of primary localized cutaneous amyloidosis. It presents as an intensely itchy rash on the shins, thighs, feet, and forearms. Lesions consist of multiple raised spots (papules) that are scaly and red/brown. Papules may coalesce into thickened plaques.

question: Reduction in the serum level of which of the following is most appropriate to treat the lesions shown in this 56-year-old man?
explanation: Recognize these small waxy papules on the extensor surfaces as features of eruptive xanthoma. These lesions are strongly associated with hyperlipidemia, for which triglyceride-lowering agents are indicated.

question: A 64-year old man develops yellowish periorbital plaques that occasionally ulcerate and heal with scarring. What is the most likely associated lab finding?
explanation: The patient has necrobiotic xanthogranuloma. Lesions develop periorbitally and in flexural areas, often extend deeply into the dermis or subcutis, and heal with scarring. These lesions are typically associated with a monoclonal gammopathy, usually IgG. Patients with necrobiotic xanthogranuloma rarely develop myeloma. Leukopenia and hepatosplenomegaly are also often seen.

question: Actinic prurigo can occur in areas that are exposed to the sun. Cheilitis is frequently seen and the treatment that has been found effective is:
explanation: Actinic prurigo can persist for months even into the winter. Lesions can occur on sun and non sun-exposed areas. Thalidomide has been very effective for the majority of patients.

question: The follicular occlusion "triad" consists of:

choices.A: Acne fulminans, hidradenitis suppurativa, and dissecting cellulitis of the scalp
choices.B: Acne conglobata, hidradenitis suppurativa, and kerion
choices.C: Acne comedonicus, hidradenitis suppurativa, and dissecting cellulitis of the scalp
choices.D: Acne conglobata, chloracne, and pyoderma faciale
choices.E: Acne conglobata, hidradenitis suppurativa, and dissecting cellulitis of the scalp

correct_text:
Acne conglobata, hidradenitis suppurativa, and dissecting cellulitis of the
scalp
explanation: Acne conglobata is a severe variant of acne vulgaris characterized by large, often multiple comedones, abscesses with sinus formation, and inflammatory nodules. Hidradenitis suppurativa is a chronic condition characterized by swollen, painful, inflamed lesions in the axillae, groin, and other parts of the body that contain apocrine glands. Dissecting cellulitis of the scalp, also known as perifolliculitis capitis abscedens et suffodiens of Hoffman, consists of deep inflammatory boggy nodules with or without sinus tracts on the occipital scalp, most commonly in African American males.

question: Ichthyosiform erythroderma in lines of Blaschko, follicular atrophoderma, and stippled epiphyses are characteristic of which of the following disorders?
explanation: Chondrodysplasia punctata is a peroxisomal disorder caused by mutations in several genes that is associated with ichthyosiform erythroderma in lines of Blaschko, follicular atrophoderma, and stippled epiphyses.

question: A patient has new-onset shortness of breath and the rash shown. She denies weakness or any other systemic symptoms. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Dermatomyositis (DM) can present as clinically amyopathic disease featuring characteristic skin changes and interstitial lung disease.

question: This is considered to be the juvenile counterpart of DFSP:
explanation: Giant cell fibroblastoma is CD34-positive, is mostly seen in male children on the neck/trunk, and is thought to be a juvenile counterpart of DFSP.

question: Pyostomatitis vegetans is characteristically associated with which systemic disease?
explanation: Pyostomatitis vegetans is a pustular, vegetative variant of pyoderma gangrenosum, found in the oral mucous membranes. It is most frequently associated with inflammatory bowel disease.

question: A 3-year-old female presents with a lipomatous overgrowth in the inguinal area, pebble-like textural changes of the skin on her left sole, leg length discrepancy, and an epidermal nevus on her abdomen. A mutation in which of the following genes is associated with this condition?
explanation: A sporadic mutation of AKT1 causes Proteus syndrome. AKT1 is an oncogene that encodes the serine-threonine protein kinase AKT. AKT is involved in cell proliferation and apoptosis through the mammalian target of the rapamycin (mTOR) signaling pathway; mutation leads to overgrowth noted in Proteus syndrome.

question: What is the most common systemic disease associated with Pyoderma Gangrenosum?
explanation: Inflammatory bowel disease is the most common disease associated with Pyoderma Gangrenosum. Ulcerative colitis is more common than Crohn's.

question: Signs of virilization include all of the following EXCEPT:

choices.E: Increased muscle mass in the limb girdles

explanation: Centripetal obesity is a sign of cortisol excess not of virilization. In addition to the those listed above, irregular or absent menses and deepening of the voice are signs of virilization.

question: Which of the following is FALSE regarding actinomycosis?

choices.A: Drainage of yellow sulfur-like granules is characteristic
choices.B: The treatment of choice is penicillin
choices.C: It most often develops on the jawline
choices.D: It is caused by an anaerobic filamentous Gram-negative bacterium
choices.E: Poor dental hygiene is a risk factor

correct_text: It is caused by an anaerobic filamentous Gram-negative bacterium
explanation: Actinomyces israelii, the causative agent of actinomycosis, is an anaerobic filamentous Gram-positive bacterium that is part of the normal oral flora.

question: Which of the following is the most characteristic radiographic finding in Type 1 Gaucher disease?
explanation: The Ehrlenmeyer-flask deformity is found in the femoral midshaft in Type 1 Gaucher disease.

question: Which drug is a frequent cause of drug-induced pemphigus?
explanation: Penicillamine is a frequent cause of drug-induced pemphigus. Other inducing drugs are thiol-containing drugs (captopril, penicillamine, thiopronine) or drugs with disulfide bonds (gold, pyritinol); also drugs that have the potential to release sulfur moieties (penicillins, piroxicam, cephalosporins), pyrazolone derivatives and enalapril (possibly secondary to an amide group), indocin, and rifampin. 75% or more are pemphigus foliaceus like (especially when secondary to thiol-drugs) and 25% resemble pemphigus vulgaris.

question: Which of the following medications is NOT associated with exacerbating this condition?
explanation: Acne or acneiform erruptions can be caused or exacerbated by corticosteroids, oral contraceptives, androgens, ACTH, lithium, phenytoin, INH, and haloperidol file:///tmp/ Quiz_Questions_1778874819.html Page 1,490 of 1,559

question: A patient with multiple hyperpigmented patches in the axillae and an optic glioma likely has which of the following disorders?
explanation: The diagnostic criteria for neurofibromatosis I include meeting 2 or more of the following 7 criteria: (1) ≥6 café au lait macules (CALMs) that are >5 mm in a prepubertal person or >15 mm in a postpubertal person, (2) >1 neurofibroma or 1 plexiform neurofibroma, (3) axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe’s sign), (4) optic glioma, (5) >1 Lisch nodule (iris hamartoma), (6) sphenoid dysplasia, (7) 1st degree relative with neurofibromatosis I.

question: A patient with end stage renal disease and on dialysis has an opaque white appearance of half of the nail. This is called:
explanation: This finding associated with end stage renal disease where half of the nail is opaque is called Lindsay's nail.

question: Which of the following is the most common secondary neoplasm in a nevus sebaceous of Jadassohn?
explanation: The most common benign neoplasm is trichoblastoma. A total of 706 patients (707 specimens) were included in a study conducted by Idriss and Elston. Trichoblastoma was the most frequent benign tumor (n = 52, 7.4%) followed by syringocystadenoma papilliferum (n = 33, 5.2%). Malignant tumors were present in 2.5% of the specimens, with basal cell carcinoma being the most common (n = 8, 1.1%) followed by squamous cell carcinoma (n = 4, 0.57%).

question: When performing a biopsy of a suspected keratoacanthoma, which of the following is incorrect?

choices.A: It is necessary to biopsy down to subcutaneous fat
choices.B: Fusiform incision through the entire KA may be performed
choices.C: A complete excisional biopsy may be performed
choices.D: It is important to biopsy the lesion, even if it is less than 1cm
choices.E: A full-thickness shave biopsy is acceptable

correct_text: It is necessary to biopsy down to subcutaneous fat
explanation: When considering a keratoacanthoma, it is not required to obtain a biopsy of the specimen down to the subcutaneous fat.

question: A 35-year-old man presents with some round to oval, hypomelanotic macules several centimeters in diameter on his back. There is associated fine scale apparent upon scratching the skin. The distribution is symmetric and is mostly on the posterior trunk and shoulders. While the contrast between the hypomelanotic infected skin and the surrounding normal skin is striking in darkly pigmented patients or following a tan in lightly

choices.B: pigmented patients, Wood's lamp examination may be required to locate all the lesions. Which of the following mechanisms does NOT play a role
choices.C: leading to decreased melanin synthesis in this condition?
choices.E: Azelaic acid ? Impairment in melanosome transfer ? Decreased number of melanosomes in keratinocytes ? Reduction of unsaturated fatty acids

correct_text:
Azelaic acid ? Impairment in melanosome transfer ? Decreased number of
melanosomes in keratinocytes ? Reduction of unsaturated fatty acids
explanation: Pityriasis versicolor (PV), also known as tinea versicolor, is a superficial fungal infection caused by conversion of Malassezia from its yeast to its mycelial form. The hypopigmented variant of PV is known as pityriasis versicolor alba (PVa). Electron microscopy of PVa lesions reveals damaged melanocytes and decreased number of melanosomes in keratinocytes, suggesting impairment in melanosome transfer. The underlying etiology is thought to involve oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids by Malassezia, leading to production of lipoperoxides and dicarboxylic acids, such as azelaic acid. These byproducts have been shown to competitively inhibit tyrosinase in vitro, thereby decreasing melanin synthesis. Conversion of tryptophan into the indole compound malassezin, which induces melanocyte apoptosis, may also play a role. On the other hand, hyperpigmented lesions (more commonly noted in lighter skin tones) may result from a hyperemic inflammatory response elicited by Malassezia species, more tonofilaments in the granulosum, a thicker stratum corneum, and abnormally large melanosomes.

question: What is the most common extracutaneous manifestation of Sweet's syndrome?
explanation: Extracutaneous manifestations of Sweet's syndrome occur in more than 75 percent of patients with Sweet's syndrome. The most common is fever, followed by arthralgias, arthritis, or myalgias. Other less frequent manifestations include conjunctivitis, episcleritis, oral aphthae-like lesions, cough, dyspnea, pleuritis, and sterile multifocal osteomyelitis. Cardiac, renal, hepatic, intestinal, or neurologic manifestations are rare.

question: Cutaneous osteomas are seen in which syndrome?
explanation: Albright hereditary osteodystrophy is caused by mutations in the Gs subunit of adenylate cyclase. There is calcification and ossification due to pseudohypoparathyroidism, absent 4th knuckle, and hypogonadism.

question: Which of the following diseases is caused by an enzymatic defect that occurs in the mitochondria?
explanation: Defects in many of the enzymes involved in heme synthesis are responsible for porphyrias. The first and last three steps of the heme synthesis pathway occur in the mitochondria.

question: Hyper IgE syndromes are associated with genetic deficiency of which of the following?
explanation: To date, three genetic etiologies of hyper IgE syndromes have been identified: STAT3, DOCK8, and Tyk2. All of these hyper IgE syndromes are characterized by eczema, sinopulmonary infections, and greatly elevated serum IgE. However, each has distinct clinical manifestations. Mutations in STAT3 cause autosomal dominant HIES (Job\'s syndrome), which is unique in its diversity of connective tissue, skeletal, and vascular abnormalities. DOCK8 deficiency is characterized by severe cutaneous viral infections such as warts, and a predisposition to malignancies at a young age. Hyper IgE syndrome associated with Tyk2 deficiency is characterized by nontuberculous mycobacterial infections.

question: All of the following are associated with anonychia or absence of the nail EXCEPT:

choices.C: Congenital onychodysplasia of the index finger

explanation: All of the following, except Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, is associated with anonychia or absence of the nail.

question: These nail findings are most likely due to infection with which organism?
explanation: The image displays the clinical features of onychomycosis. T. rubrum is the most common cause of onychomycosis in the US.

question: Which of the following statements is true regarding this entity?

choices.A: Atopic dermatitis is a predictor of good prognosis
choices.C: The inner root sheath and matrix of normal hair express MHC class I
choices.D: The sisapho pattern involves the occipital scalp
choices.E: 80% of patients with early onset disease have a positive family history

explanation: Twin concordance (identical twins) is 55% in alopecia areata.

question: A patient with renal amyloidosis, urticaria, fevers, limb pains, and deafness is diagnosed with Muckle-Wells syndrome after genetic testing. What is the mutation identified?
explanation: Muckle-Wells is an autosomal dominant condition with mutation in the NLRP3 (CIAS1) gene. It is characterized by "attacks" that last for 1-2 days with urticarial papules and plaques that are widespread on the face, trunk, and extremities. Patients experience abdominal pain, severe myalgias and arthritis, conjunctivitis, episcleritis, optic disc edema, sensorineural hearing loss, and headache. It is associated with AA amyloid protein. It is important to note that Muckle-Wells syndrome is one of three syndromes that fall into the category of cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPs). Other syndromes included in this category are familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome and familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome. CAPs are also part of a larger category called hereditary periodic fever syndromes, which includes familial Mediterranean fever, hyperimmunoglobulinemia D with periodic fever syndrome, and TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome.

question: Periorificial dermatitis is thought to be a variant of rosacea. What is a known association with periorificial dermatitis?
explanation: Periorificial dermatitis (or perioral dermatitis) has been associated with prior use of topical or inhaled fluorinated steroids, therefore they should be discontinued.

question: Gap junctions consist of:
explanation: Gap junctions are protein channels that allow for communcation between cells. A connexon of one cell is joined to that of an adjacent cell to form an intercellular channel consisting of 12 connexin subunits. Each intercellular channel provides a channel that interconnects the cytoplasm of the apposed cell directly and permits the passage of ion and other small molecules between adjacent cells. These protein channels that make up the gap junctions consist of two hemi-channels or connexons. One connexon resides in the membrane of one cell and it aligns and joins the connexon of the neighboring cell, forming a continuous aquaeous pathway by which these ions and small molecules can freely pass from one cell to the other. Each hemi-channel or connexon consist of six proteins ( hexamer) called connexins.

question: A 65-year-old patient presents with this painful, itchy rash on the right dorsal foot. The pain has made ambulating difficult. Prior unsuccessful treatments included topical betamethasone and clotrimazole. Based on the image provided, which of the following treatments have the highest cure rate?

choices.E: Topical ciclopirox nail lacquer ? Oral itraconazole

explanation: The correct answer is oral terbinafine. This patient has onychomycosis complicated by severe tinea pedis/incognito. The combination of betamethasone and clotrimazole allowed the fungus to spread to the dorsal and lateral aspects of the right foot. A nail clipping was sent to pathology, which confirmed the presence of dermatophytes in the nail plate. When treating tinea, it is important to address the onychomycosis as well, this is to prevent recurrences. The patient had greater than three nails affected, so oral therapy is indicated to treat both the onychomycosis and tinea pedis. Systemic treatments approved for onychomycosis include oral terbinafine and itraconazole. Due to higher cure rates with terbinafine and fewer drug interactions, terbinafine is usually preferred over itraconazole. For the toenails, terbinafine and itraconazole have a complete cure rate of 38% and 14%, respectively. Terbinafine’s most common side effects are headache, gastrointestinal symptoms, and rash. Terbinafine-induced idiosyncratic liver injury is rare: the FDA recommends baseline serum transaminases but data are lacking on laboratory monitoring.

question: A 25 year-old previously healthy man presents with the skin findings shown, urethritis, and one month of peripheral arthritis. Which of the following is true regarding this condition?

choices.A: A chronic deforming arthritis occurs in 20%
choices.B: Chlamydia cervicitis is not associated with this condition
choices.C: Patients must have urethritis, conjunctivitis, and arthritis for diagnosis
choices.D: TNF-alpha inhibiting agents have no role in the treatment of this condition
choices.E: Females and males are equally affected

correct_text: A chronic deforming arthritis occurs in 20%
explanation: The patient has reactive arthritis.
